## Current role

Senior Solutions Engineer at Offsight since September 2022. Offsight is a production
and quality tracking platform used by prefab and modular construction
manufacturers to track production status, quality issues, materials, and labor
across factory stations. He runs technical discovery, designs workflow
configurations and integrations, leads end-to-end client onboarding, trains
client teams, tests and helps shape the product itself, and advises executives
on where their operational bottlenecks are.

## Who he works with

**Manufacturers** — modular, prefab, and offsite builders. Operational
assessment, quality and compliance systems, software selection and rollout,
training that holds after go-live, and owner's representation on projects.

**Software companies** — teams building for manufacturing and construction who
want someone who has actually run a plant. Technical discovery and solutions
engineering, product requirements and workflow design, release validation and
usability testing, onboarding programs, and customer success.

## Measured results

- 50%+ reduction in average client implementation time (Offsight)
- 30% reduction in rework through end-to-end QA systems (as Quality Control Manager)
- 25% increase in user adoption across key accounts
- 15% shorter project completion timelines via streamlined third-party inspections
- 20% higher post-delivery satisfaction scores
- 38% year-over-year territory sales growth in 2015

## Work history

- **Senior Solutions Engineer**, Offsight — 2022–present
- **Quality Control Manager**, Volumetric Building Companies — 2019–2022
- **Service Manager**, Ritz-Craft Custom Homes → Volumetric Building Companies — 2018–2019
- **District Manager**, CZ Wireless — 2016–2018
- **Regional Account Manager**, Ritz-Craft Custom Homes — 2015–2016
- **Store Manager**, AT&T / Alltel Wireless — 2011–2015
- **Sales Representative → Assistant Store Manager**, Alltel Wireless — 2001–2011

Twenty-plus years leading teams. He has worked inside modular and prefab
manufacturing since 2015, and spent 14 years in wireless retail leadership
before that, including a key role in a billing migration affecting 600,000+
customers.

## Six disciplines

1. **Solutions engineering** — technical discovery, requirements translation,
   demonstrations connecting what the floor needs to what the software does.
2. **Operations and quality management** — end-to-end QA systems built inside a
   volumetric modular plant, meeting building codes, engineering specs, and
   customer requirements.
3. **Training and leadership development** — workshops where participants hit
   competency benchmarks in month one; supervisor coaching; sales training
   programs built from scratch.
4. **Implementation management** — end-to-end onboarding run as a managed
   project with executive stakeholders, not a support ticket.
5. **AI engineering** — building internal tools, automations, documentation,
   and reporting with AI, and applying AI inside manufacturing operations.
6. **Software QA and product design** — functional, regression, workflow, and
   end-to-end validation before releases ship, plus requirements, feature
   priorities, and role-based functionality defined with the development team.

## Capabilities

**Operations and quality:** operational excellence and continuous improvement;
manufacturing operations across the full lifecycle (estimating, engineering,
purchasing, scheduling, production, quality, shipping, installation, warranty,
service); production systems and workflow design; quality management and CAPA;
compliance and regulatory systems including QA manuals, document control,
modular certification programs, and state requirements; training and knowledge
transfer.

**Software and product:** solutions engineering; implementation and digital
transformation; software QA and product validation; product development and
requirements; software design and UX; AI strategy and engineering.

**Business and leadership:** executive leadership and business strategy;
business process analysis; project management; data, reporting, and business
intelligence; executive communication; customer success and consultative sales.

## Consulting methodology

A repeatable framework: discovery, operational assessment, workflow analysis,
stakeholder interviews, software evaluation, process mapping, improvement
recommendations, implementation planning, training, and long-term support.

His implementation work specifically runs in three stages — Discovery (days on
the floor walking every station and timing handoffs), Configuration (data
capture, stations, QC checkpoints, and material tracking modeled on the
sequence crews already work), and Adoption (supervisors trained first so they
can coach, then operators in station, with competency measured against
benchmarks).

## Case studies

Three engagements on the site show the method end to end. Clients are kept
anonymous.

1. **Panelized manufacturer — software implementation.** Production ran on
   paper and memory. Four days of discovery on the floor; production tracking
   configured to the line in week one; supervisors trained first, then
   operators in station. Crews owned the process by week four with no paper
   left on the production floor.

2. **Volumetric modular factory and developer — operational
   foundation.** The factory was scaling, rolling out digital production
   tracking, and strengthening state compliance at once. A four-day phase-one
   assessment covered fourteen departments; the quality and compliance program
   was modernized for usability and state modular requirements; eight
   deliverables ran from current-state assessment to an accountability
   framework, with leaders coached into owning the procedures.

3. **Panelized manufacturing division of a national construction manager —
   operational assessment.** Four days observing fourteen production processes
   exactly as they operated. Six compounding findings (tribal knowledge,
   excessive motion, material prep stealing assembly labor, reactive quality,
   underused equipment, inconsistent training) and a prioritized roadmap
   across seven categories, sequenced so improvement never stops production.

## Owner's representative

Available to serve as an Owner's Representative or Owner's Agent on modular and
prefab construction projects, protecting the owner's interests. He has run
quality from inside a plant and worked the vendor side implementing operational
technology, so he can read what a manufacturer or supplier is telling you.

Alongside the manufacturing work, he handles day-to-day practice management for

## Writing

An article, "Why most manufacturing software implementations fail, and how to
prevent it," is published at
https://jasoncdixon.com/why-implementations-fail.html. It covers five reasons
implementations struggle (wrong implementation leadership, no subject matter
expert, poor planning, overlooked hardware/Wi-Fi/IT infrastructure, and
software that stops being used as a management tool), two real-world examples,
and nine best practices. The full nine-page white paper is available on the
page after a short request form.

## Operating principle

Sustainable performance comes from strong systems, not harder pushing. Clear
processes, reliable data, disciplined execution, and accountability at every
level. What makes his vantage point unusual is that he built quality systems
from the inside as a QC manager and now implements operational technology from
the outside, so he understands both how factories run and how to make tools
serve the way they run.
